guides.title: How the Live Bitcoin Price Updates | PRICEB.TC
guides.heading: How the Bitcoin price updates
guides.description: Understand the Coinbase BTC/USD feed, price timestamps, delayed data and daily currency conversions used by PRICEB.TC.
sections: Where the price comes from

PRICEB.TC displays BTC/USD market data from Coinbase Exchange, including the current price, 24-hour high/low, and trading volume. These metrics reflect activity on the Coinbase BTC-USD market only—not aggregated global exchange data. Different exchanges can quote different prices and volumes because their order books and trades are independent.
Updates and timestamps

The running service receives market updates and sends them to connected browsers. The displayed UTC time is the market timestamp of the latest observation, not the time you opened the page. The initial page includes the latest available USD snapshot; JavaScript keeps it current afterward. There is no guaranteed update frequency or latency.
Live, delayed and unavailable

A recent received snapshot is marked live; a snapshot older than 15 seconds is stale. Connection problems can also show delayed data. A delayed quote remains useful as a last observation, but it is not a current trading quote. If no snapshot exists, the page reports that the price is unavailable.
Currencies and chart windows

USD is the direct market quote. Other supported currencies use indicative daily ExchangeRate-API conversions, so they can differ from local exchange prices. The 1h, 24h and 7d chart windows display historical price and volume data (BTC base volume) from Coinbase Exchange. Volume bars are shown for USD; converted currency views display price only. The headline 24h change and a selected chart window change can differ.
Buy and sell volume

Green and red volume segments show recorded buyer-initiated and seller-initiated BTC trades on Coinbase Exchange. Each trade has both a buyer and a seller; the classification identifies the side taking liquidity. Coinbase reports the maker side, which PRICEB.TC reverses to identify the initiating side. This is not inferred from whether the price rose or fell. The service checks recent trades every 10 seconds and retains minute aggregates for eight days; the chart refreshes every 30 seconds. Only retrieved trades are classified. Grey volume has no recorded split, and older intervals or gaps may be incomplete. Candle totals and recorded trades can update at different times.
Reading prices with an agent

Use the public JSON endpoints described below for a timestamped observation. Keep the source, currency and status with the number. Do not describe stale data as live or treat the page request time as the market time.

guides.title: Free Bitcoin Price Widget for Your Website | PRICEB.TC
guides.heading: Add a Bitcoin price widget to your website
guides.description: Create a free Bitcoin price widget, choose a layout and currency, then copy the iframe into your website. No account required.
sections: Build a widget

Open Widget Studio and choose Website Embed. Select a layout, currency and the content you want to show. Adjust appearance while watching the preview; the preview and export use the same configuration.
Copy and publish

Copy the generated iframe from Studio. Paste it into a custom HTML block or your page markup. Publish the page and check its desktop and mobile layouts. The widget needs network access and JavaScript to receive current prices.
A working starting point

The example below embeds the USD renderer. For customized colors, dimensions and layout, use the complete export generated by Studio. Keep the iframe title so assistive technology can identify the widget.
Check the published result

If your editor removes the iframe, use its supported custom HTML or embed feature. If the widget cannot load, check your website’s frame policy and network restrictions. Give the frame enough space for the selected layout and test long prices on mobile.
Price source and sponsorship

Widgets use the same Coinbase price source and indicative currency conversions as the homepage. They are free and require no account. Future sponsor examples shown on the homepage are illustrative; they are not active sponsor placements inside current exported widgets.

guides.title: Bitcoin Price OBS Overlay Setup Guide | PRICEB.TC
guides.heading: Put the Bitcoin price on your OBS stream
guides.description: Set up a transparent Bitcoin price overlay in OBS using a Browser Source. Customize the layout and currency in the free PRICEB.TC Studio.
sections: Create your overlay
Open Widget Studio and choose OBS Overlay. Pick a layout and currency, customize the appearance, and inspect the transparent preview. Copy the OBS source URL generated by Studio.
Add a Browser Source
In OBS, add a Browser Source to your scene. Paste the copied URL into its URL field. Use the width and height shown in Studio for your chosen layout, then position and scale the source in your scene.
Transparency and readability

The overlay renderer supports a transparent background. Preview it over both bright and dark footage. Choose enough contrast for the price and labels and leave padding around the source so text is not cropped.
Troubleshooting

If nothing appears, confirm the URL opens in a regular browser and that OBS has network access. Refresh the Browser Source after changing its URL. If text is clipped, increase the source dimensions to match the export. Delayed data can reflect an upstream connection issue; check the homepage status before assuming the overlay is broken.
Before going live

Record a short test and inspect it at your stream resolution. Keep the source attribution and data status legible. The overlay shows market information, not a guaranteed buy or sell price. Other broadcasting tools with a Browser Source may also work; verify the result in your own setup.
